pr_body:
**kvserver/rangefeed: lift CrdbTestBuild on RangefeedUseBufferedSender**

This patch removes the buildutil.CRDBTestBuild check for
RangefeedUseBufferedSender, as the feature is now fully
implemented and safe to use without causing panics.

Epic: none
Release note: none

---

**roachtest: use prng to enable RangefeedUseBufferedSender**

Previously, we used UsingRuntimeAssertions to determine whether
to enable RangefeedUseBufferedSender because it was gated behind
the CRDBTestBuild flag. Now that this check has been removed,
we can use prng to enable the cluster setting 50% of the time.

Note that we still need to avoid enabling the cluster setting
for mixed-version roachtests to prevent it from being applied
to versions that enforce this restriction.

Epic: none
Fixes: #141478
Fixes: #141470
Fixes: #141494
Fixes: #141476
FIxes: #141466
Fixes: #141470
Fixes: #141471
Fixes: #141475
Fixes: #141465

review_comments: `UsingRuntimeAssertions` was previously gating benchmark tests from enabling buffered sender. We should probably still disable buffered senders on benchmark tests? Unless you expect there to be no performance impact.

We don’t anticipate negative performance impact (at least we hope), and it would be good to verify if there’s any regression. If we feel strongly about this, the simplest approach might be to opt into this cluster setting when `registry.MetamorphicLeases` is enabled as that registry.TestSpec tries to achieve the same thing 
https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/commit/fc68b0fe8d967ab48d96a659fd5a067787e5e734.

My concern is less about negative regressions and more about increased variance in benchmark results. i.e. someone working on improving sysbench perf would need to both know about this metamorphic setting and make sure to conditionally enable/disable it or their results will fluctuate more than expected.

That being said I'm not familiar with this work at all so I'll defer to your judgement if you think the perf impact is minimal.

I see, that's a good point. I would need to look closer at what the sysbench perf team is analyzing to provide a better answer. I would expect the perf impact to be minimal if the tests they are running don't use testRunner or enable `kv.rangefeed.enabled` but not sure otherwise.

Update: Chatted with Darryl and we are not worried about ^ given roachperf has been fine and only ldr pcr cdc roachtests use rangefeeds.
